summary: Primary-source archaeology materially narrows four active-batch gates without editing canonical state. RKLB's liquidity/dilution picture is now quantitatively anchored through Q2 2026 but remains financing-dependent by design; ARM's SoftBank control/related-party and customer-concentration gate is strongly quantified; ASML's China/export-mix gate is materially narrowed while critical-supplier concentration remains unresolved; ANET's large-customer concentration and white-box/custom-network substitution gate is directly supported by its latest 10-Q.

targets.exactResearchQuestionGate: fresh filing-level loss/cash-burn, dilution/acquisition-accounting normalization and Neutron qualification/schedule risk
targets.summary: Q2 2026 SEC evidence closes much of the cash-burn/dilution side of the gate. Rocket Lab held $2.129B cash plus $258.1M marketable securities at June 30, 2026, while six-month operating cash use was $134.4M and investing cash use was $84.6M. This strong gross liquidity was funded in material part by equity issuance: 6.727M shares generated $474.0M gross under the terminated March 2026 distribution agreement and another 7.783M shares generated $1.056B gross under the May 2026 agreement. Collared forwards add 7.451M underlying shares with $474M-$642M expected proceeds at April 2028 maturities. Neutron remains in qualification/integration and management explicitly warns further delays can require additional R&D/capex.

findings.claim: At June 30, 2026 Rocket Lab reported $2.129B cash and cash equivalents and $258.1M marketable securities; six-month operating cash use was $134.4M and investing cash use was $84.6M.

During the first six months of 2026 Rocket Lab sold 6,726,862 common shares for $474.009M gross under the terminated March 2026 distribution agreement and 7,783,458 common shares for $1.05563B gross under the May 2026 distribution agreement.
The March 2026 collared forward transactions cover 7,451,200 shares with minimum expected proceeds of about $474M and maximum expected proceeds of about $642M, scheduled around April 2028 maturities.

Neutron qualification testing and first-flight integration were still ongoing in Q2 2026; the filing states additional delays or setbacks may require more R&D and capital expenditures than currently anticipated.

Near-term solvency/runway risk is substantially lower than the historical loss profile alone implies, but the 2026 liquidity build cannot be interpreted as internally funded operating strength because equity/forward financing contributed far more cash than operating burn consumed. Any normalized capital-survival score should separate operating cash generation from financing capacity.

contradictions: Large absolute liquidity coexists with continued operating cash burn, acquisition spend and explicit willingness to raise/refinance opportunistically.
Neutron hardware progress is real, but qualification, first-flight schedule and production-cadence risk remain explicitly unresolved by management.
unknowns: Exact fully diluted denominator after combining outstanding common stock, preferred conversion, employee awards, ATM shares and collared-forward settlement mechanics without double-counting.
A source-grounded Neutron first-flight probability/schedule distribution and remaining program cash requirement.
Acquisition purchase-price accounting normalization for Mynaric/Motiv and any contingent consideration not yet fully bridged into a normalized operating view.
falsifiers: A material Neutron qualification failure or schedule reset that raises expected development cash needs materially above current disclosures.
Evidence that the 2026 equity/forward issuance substantially understates effective dilution due to additional in-the-money awards or acquisition-linked instruments.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: Reconcile the June 30, 2026 equity footnotes, cover-page share count, 2021 Plan/ESPP reserves and collared-forward settlement terms into one fully diluted bridge; separately pull Neutron qualification/launch-license primary records before promotion.

targets.exactResearchQuestionGate: related-party economics, SoftBank/control governance and customer-concentration durability
targets.summary: The FY2026 20-F and June 2026 interim filing strongly quantify this gate. SoftBank beneficially owned about 86.4% of Arm as of May 21, 2026; 769.029M shares representing 72.0% were pledged under a SoftBank financing facility. The shareholder governance agreement permits extensive board-designation and consent rights. Top five customers represented 57% of FY2026 revenue, Arm China alone 16%, and three customers collectively represented 42%. Related-party revenue was $1.499B in FY2026 versus $823M in FY2025; June-quarter 2026 consulting-agreement revenue from a SoftBank affiliate was $192.9M with $577.2M of current/non-current contract assets from that affiliate.

findings.claim: SoftBank beneficially owned approximately 922.734M Arm shares, about 86.4% of issued share capital, as of May 21, 2026; 769.029M shares representing 72.0% were pledged under the SoftBank Group Facility.
Arm's FY2026 top five customers collectively represented about 57% of revenue and Arm China alone about 16%; three customers individually represented 16%, 14% and 12%, or 42% combined.
FY2026 related-party revenue was $1.499B compared with $823M in FY2025, including $1.009B of license/other revenue and $490M of royalty revenue from related parties.

For the June 2026 quarter, revenue under the SoftBank consulting agreement was $192.9M versus $126.1M a year earlier; contract assets tied to a SoftBank affiliate totaled about $577.2M at June 30, 2026.

SoftBank governance rights include extensive board designation, committee/transaction rights and pre-emptive rights; Arm explicitly warns SoftBank interests may conflict with Arm or ADS holders and that foreclosure/sale of pledged shares could cause a change of control.

The gate should not be modeled as ordinary customer concentration only: monetization concentration and control concentration overlap because SoftBank/affiliates are simultaneously controller, governance counterparty and material commercial counterparty. This deserves explicit governance/conflict and customer-dependency penalties rather than being averaged away across separate rubric factors.

contradictions: Arm's broad ecosystem adoption coexists with concentrated accounting revenue and unusually concentrated corporate control.
Related-party revenue growth materially boosts reported growth while increasing dependence on transactions where Arm itself discloses potential conflicts of interest.
unknowns: Economic durability of the newer SoftBank-affiliate license/consulting arrangements after their initial contractual periods.
Exact identity of the non-Arm-China customers comprising the 14% and 12% FY2026 concentration buckets where the filing does not publicly name them.
Whether SoftBank's pledged-share facility loan-to-value thresholds create a realistically material forced-sale probability under severe ADS drawdown scenarios.
falsifiers: Sustained decline in related-party share of revenue while external-customer royalty growth remains strong would reduce the dependency penalty.
A material SoftBank ownership reduction accompanied by termination of enhanced governance rights would weaken the control-risk thesis.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: Chief/underwriting can now promote the quantified ownership, pledge, related-party revenue and customer-concentration facts after checking for any later ownership filing; keep durability and unnamed-customer identity explicitly unknown.

targets.exactResearchQuestionGate: China/export mix and quantified critical-supplier concentration
targets.summary: The China/export half of the gate is materially narrowed with current primary evidence. China represented 29.1% of 2025 total net sales, down from 36.1% in 2024. Q2 2026 net-system sales shipped to China were 14% versus 19% in Q1 2026, while Taiwan and South Korea together represented 73% of Q2 net-system sales. ASML's 2025 annual report explicitly states EUV, specified DUV immersion and other products require export licenses and that licensing criteria are outside ASML's control. Critical-supplier concentration remains only qualitatively established: ASML reports roughly 900 product-related suppliers and calls supplier partnerships essential, but the reviewed primary sources do not quantify revenue/output exposure to named critical suppliers.

findings.claim: Customers in China represented 29.1% of ASML's 2025 total net sales versus 36.1% in 2024.
Q2 2026 net-system sales by ship-to location were 14% China, 30% Taiwan, 43% South Korea and 9% USA; Q1 2026 China was 19%.
ASML states export licenses are required for EUV, specified DUV immersion and some other products and that government licensing scope/criteria can change outside ASML's control.

ASML reports about 900 product-related suppliers plus roughly 4,200 non-product-related suppliers and describes the supply chain as essential to product design and delivery, but the reviewed annual-report material does not provide a usable named-supplier percentage concentration table.

China exposure has fallen materially in the observable sales mix, so a static 2024-style China concentration penalty would overstate current geographic revenue exposure. Export-control risk nevertheless remains structural because restrictions apply by technology/entity and can affect future service/system availability independent of current quarter mix.

contradictions: Current China sales mix is lower, but regulatory optionality remains outside management control and therefore cannot be inferred away from the lower percentage.
A broad supplier count does not prove low concentration: highly specialized lithography modules may remain dependent on a small number of technically irreplaceable suppliers.
unknowns: Quantified exposure to named critical/sole-source suppliers by bill-of-material value, system throughput or substitution lead time.
How much of Q2 2026 China exposure is service/field-option versus new-system exposure in a way that maps directly to future export-control sensitivity.
falsifiers: Primary supplier disclosures showing rapid qualified second-source substitution for the highest-complexity optical/mechatronic modules would weaken the supplier-bottleneck thesis.
A renewed rise in China share combined with tighter licensing would reverse the observed geographic de-risking trend.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: Search ASML supplier-framework disclosures, strategic-supplier/JV filings and named critical suppliers' annual reports for sole-source status, ASML revenue dependence, capacity commitments and substitution lead times; do not mark the supplier-concentration gate closed until quantitatively defensible.

targets.exactResearchQuestionGate: filing-level large-customer concentration and white-box/custom-network substitution evidence
targets.summary: The latest Q2 2026 10-Q directly closes the evidence-acquisition portion of this gate. Two end customers represented 16% and 26% of 2025 revenue, or 42% combined; the same two represented 15%/20% in 2024 and 21%/18% in 2023. Arista states large customers generally receive higher discounts and that this mix contributed to six-month 2026 gross-margin compression to 62.4% from 64.5%. The filing explicitly names white-box/open-source networking, vertically integrated competitors, cloud providers/customers developing switches internally, and even merchant-silicon partners as substitution/competition risks. It also identifies Broadcom as the predominant merchant-silicon vendor, creating a supplier/competitor dependency.

findings.claim: Two end customers represented 16% and 26% of 2025 revenue, 15% and 20% in 2024, and 21% and 18% in 2023.

Arista's six-month 2026 gross margin declined to 62.4% from 64.5% a year earlier, with the company citing a higher proportion of sales to large end customers who receive higher discounts as the primary driver.

Arista explicitly identifies white-box networking using open-source operating systems, vertically integrated networking solutions, cloud service providers/customers developing switches internally and new AI-networking entrants as competitive/substitution risks.
Arista identifies Broadcom as its predominant merchant-silicon vendor and warns that merchant-silicon vendors may also compete by supplying white-box solutions to Arista customers.

Customer concentration is not merely a volatility risk; it already has observable pricing/margin consequences. The substitution gate is also structurally two-sided: Arista depends on merchant silicon to focus R&D on EOS/software differentiation, while the same silicon ecosystem lowers entry barriers for white-box/custom alternatives.

contradictions: Strong AI-networking demand and rapid product growth coexist with purchasing concentration high enough to affect margins and forecasting reliability.
Merchant-silicon leverage accelerates Arista's innovation model while simultaneously enabling potential substitutes.
unknowns: Public identity of the two >10% end customers in the latest filing if not otherwise independently sourced.
Share of AI-networking deployments where customers use internally developed/custom networking rather than Arista, and whether that share is rising.
Quantitative switching costs attributable specifically to EOS/CloudVision versus hardware economics.
falsifiers: Sustained reduction of the top-two customer share without margin deterioration would weaken the concentration penalty.
Evidence that white-box/custom networking adoption remains immaterial in Arista's target AI clusters despite hyperscaler internal development would weaken the substitution thesis.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: Underwriting can now use the filing-level concentration and substitution evidence. Next, corroborate customer identities only from primary/counterparty sources and seek deployment-level evidence on custom networking versus EOS stickiness; do not infer customer names from market rumor.
